newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude off, but signs of firmer differentials.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude off, but signs of firmer differentials.

text.p: Asian crude prices were lower on Monday but differentials appeared to find some support heading into this week.
Traders said two Oman deals had been heard at MPM flat, while a Lower Zakum and a Murban were also heard done at premiums.
Traders said there could be some support for ADNOC differentials after ADNOC over the weekend cut February official selling prices between $2.75 and $2.90, helping to improve buyers sentiment.
Traders were still waiting on the release of Saudi Arabian and Oman official selling prices.
Traders said they expected the Dubai market to come under some pressure after India awarded just two cargoes in its April buying tender.
Traders said they expected the Dubai market to come under some pressure after India awarded just two cargoes in its April buying tender.
Total was awarded at half-month quotes plus 42 cents and Phibro at half-month quotes plus 44 cents. That left at least one European major exposed with two Dubais after its tender offer was declined.
The bid and offer in the wet market remained at 40 to 45 cents, little changed from late last week, but traders said the Dubai cargoes could weigh on the market.
India also awarded two VLCCs of Qua Iboe to Vitol at dated Brent +88.8 cents and +90.8 cents.

Late in the day Oman official selling prices were released, showing a narrowing spread against Dubai to $1.05 per barrel from $1.14 a month earlier. ADNOC grades came in more than 20 cents against Dubai.
Minas remained depressed, being talked around ICP -50/70 cents as affiliates and equity holders looked at diplomatic ways to reject further export allocations from Pertamina.
Duri was discussed around ICP -50/60 cents, with some demand showing for fuel oil blending. --Singapore, N.Fullick (+65 870 3081), Tokyo, M.Yoshikawa (+813 5473 3706)
